lookahead.title: Lookahead analysis
lookahead.subtitle: Check whether a strategy peeks at future candles by accident.
lookahead.intro: Checks your strategy for lookahead bias by comparing signals generated on the full dataset against signals generated on progressively shorter timeranges. Indicators or signals that change depending on future data indicate a lookahead bias that will make backtest results unreliable.
lookahead.minTradesHint: Minimum number of trades the analysis should run for before evaluating bias.
lookahead.targetTradesHint: Targeted number of trades the analysis tries to reach. Must be greater than or equal to the minimum trade amount.
lookahead.allowLimitHint: Allow limit orders in lookahead analysis (could cause false positives in lookahead analysis results).
lookahead.noBiasHint: The strategy produced consistent signals across the analyzed timeranges.
lookahead.biasHint: The strategy produced different signals depending on the available data. Backtest results for this strategy are likely unreliable.

recursive.title: Recursive analysis
recursive.subtitle: Check whether indicator values depend on how much history is loaded.
recursive.intro: Checks your strategy's indicators for recursive formula issues by comparing indicator values calculated with different startup candle counts. Indicators that show a difference are likely affected by the amount of startup data and may produce inconsistent results between backtesting and dry/live runs.
recursive.startupCandlesHint: Comma separated list of startup candle counts to compare against each other. Leave empty to use the backend defaults.
recursive.noIssuesHint: None of the strategy indicators changed when varying the startup candle count.
recursive.affected: {count} indicator(s) affected by startup candle count
recursive.affectedHint: The values below show the percentage difference compared to the analysis with the most startup candles. Non-zero values indicate a recursive formula issue.

how.title: How the bot decides
how.exit: It sells half once the coin is 20% above the buy price, and the rest when the coin drops below its lowest price of the last 10 hours, or at the safety stop. It checks every 15 minutes. Emergency brake: after 6 safety stops within 24 hours it pauses buying for 12 hours.

mood.title: Market mood
mood.text: It only buys while Bitcoin is in an uptrend (above its 50 day average). Otherwise it waits in cash.

breakout.title: Breakout
breakout.text: A coin must rise above its highest price of the last 20 hours: a sign that a move is starting.

volume.title: Volume check
volume.text: The breakout only counts if at least twice the usual trading volume is behind it. This filters out fake breakouts.

sentinel.title: Sentinel news check
sentinel.text: Before buying, Sentinel, our AI news model, reads fresh headlines and blocks the buy on serious bad news (hack, delisting, lawsuit). If you switch AI leverage on, it may also borrow up to 3× when the news is clearly good.

result.overTwoYearsSame: over 2 years in the same test
result.disclaimer: Past results are not a promise. The test uses real price history; the future can behave differently.

live.title: Does it work in real life?
live.closedSince: {n} trade closed since the new strategy started on {date}. | {n} trades closed since the new strategy started on {date}.
live.enough: That is enough to compare: green means live matches the test.
live.tooEarly: That is too early: around 30 closed trades are needed before this comparison means anything. Until then it is only a trend.

tested.title: Before and after
tested.simple: Surprise: “locking in profit early” (trailing and breakeven stops) made things much worse. This strategy earns from a few big moves; cutting them early destroys that.
tested.pro: Both versions tested on two independent years (rising and falling market); the live strategy also on real Hyperliquid data. Other ideas we tried are summarised in docs/STRATEGY.md.

goLive.note: Coins the bot holds in practice stay in practice. With real money it starts fresh and sets its safety stops directly on Hyperliquid, so they work even if this computer is off.

confirm.disconnectMessage: The bot forgets its trading permission for this wallet. Your money stays on Hyperliquid untouched.
confirm.backMessage: The bot stops using real money and continues with pretend money. Your USDC stays in your Hyperliquid account.

practice.subtitle: Pretend money the bot practises with. Add more whenever you like, or start over.

practice.onTop: What the bot has won or lost comes on top of this.

practice.cleanSlate: Want a clean slate with a new amount?

practice.addConfirmMessage:
Your practice money goes from {from} to {to}.

The bot restarts for about a minute to pick it up. Coins it holds right now stay where they are. With more practice money, the bot makes bigger practice trades.
practice.addedToast: Practice money added. The bot now practises with {amount}.

reset.title: Start practice over?
reset.text: The bot starts again from day one with a new amount of practice money. It restarts for about a minute. Coins it holds in practice stay behind in the old history.
reset.ack: Start with a fresh practice history. The old one is kept but no longer shown.

aiLeverage.loadError: The leverage setting could not be loaded.
aiLeverage.label: Let Sentinel choose leverage (up to {max}×)
aiLeverage.statusLocked: Locked: every new trade uses 1× (no borrowing).
aiLeverage.statusOn: On: Sentinel picks 1× to {max}× for each new trade.
aiLeverage.statusOff: Off: every new trade uses 1× (no borrowing).
aiLeverage.slowBack: The bot is taking longer than usual to come back; it should be ready in a minute or two.
aiLeverage.offMessage:
New trades use 1× again (no borrowing). Coins the bot already holds keep their leverage.

The bot restarts for about a minute to apply this.
aiLeverage.explainNews: Sentinel is the AI that reads the news before every buy. With this on, it may also borrow to make a new trade bigger: 2× when the news about the coin is clearly good, 3× when Bitcoin is strong too. Without clear news it stays at 1×.
aiLeverage.explainRisk: Borrowing makes wins and losses bigger. In a fast crash the price can jump past the safety stop, and the exchange can close a borrowed trade with a total loss of the money in it (liquidation).
aiLeverage.compactRisk: Borrowing makes wins and losses bigger (2× doubles them, 3× triples them).
aiLeverage.newOnly: Changes only affect new trades. Coins the bot already holds keep their leverage.
aiLeverage.manualHint: You can still pick a leverage yourself when you buy a coin by hand.
aiLeverage.restartingTitle: The bot is restarting with the new setting
aiLeverage.restartingText: This takes about a minute. Coins it holds stay where they are.

confirm.title: Let Sentinel borrow up to 3×?
confirm.intro: For each new trade, Sentinel may borrow to make it bigger: 2× when the news about the coin is clearly good, {max}× when Bitcoin is strong too.
confirm.bigger: Wins and losses get bigger: 2× doubles them, 3× triples them. At 3×, a 5% price move becomes a 15% gain or loss on that trade's money.
confirm.crash: In a fast crash the price can jump past the safety stop. The exchange then closes the trade and all the money in it is lost (liquidation).
confirm.newOnly: Only new trades are affected. You can turn it off again at any time. The bot restarts for about a minute.
confirm.live: The bot is trading real money right now.
confirm.practice: The bot is using practice money right now. The setting stays when you switch to real money.
confirm.ack: I understand that leverage can lose more money, up to all the money in a trade.
